title: Stem cells; Gas exchange surfaces and SA:V in organisms
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE08b#t2 term and clue written for the game; EX01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE08b#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE08b#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE08b#N.5, EX01a#N.7a, EX01a#N.10, EX01a#N.11a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Adult stem cells
items.clue: Found in bone marrow, for example; make a limited range of types and can come from the patient

items.label: Surface area to volume ratio
items.clue: Key number comparing supply across the outside with demand from living tissue; falls as size rises

items.label: Embryonic stem cells
items.clue: Taken from the inner mass of an early IVF spare, which is destroyed; can form any type of body tissue

items.label: Induced pluripotent stem cells
items.clue: Reprogrammed from mature body tissue to behave as if taken from an early embryo, though none is needed

questions.stem: Bone marrow transplants are used to treat leukaemia. Which statement explains how a transplant replaces the patient's blood cells?

options.text: The donor marrow's stem cells can become any body cell, so they replace any damaged tissue.
Mature red blood cells in the donor marrow divide to make all the new blood cells.
Donor stem cells divide and differentiate to give every type of blood cell.
Donor white blood cells switch into red blood cells when the patient needs more.

questions.explanation: Blood stem cells renew themselves and differentiate into red cells, white cells and platelet-forming cells, rebuilding the patient's blood supply.

questions.stem: Why does gas exchange become a greater challenge as organisms increase in size?

options.text: The surface area-to-volume ratio increases, so far more gas has to cross each unit of the exchange surface.
The surface area-to-volume ratio decreases, and the distance from the centre of the organism to its exterior increases.
Only animals with lungs or gills exchange gases, so the challenge arises once an organism is big enough to have them.
A large organism uses more oxygen in total; the distance gases must diffuse to reach its cells makes no difference.

questions.explanation: Proportionally less surface supplies each unit of volume, and inner cells are too far away for diffusion alone. Both make specialised exchange surfaces and transport systems necessary.

questions.stem: Use the data on the mouse, human and elephant. Which statement is supported by the data?

options.text: The mouse uses more energy each day than the elephant, since its rate per kg is far higher.
Each kg of body uses energy at about the same rate in all three, so total use is proportional to mass.
Each kg of mouse uses energy about 13 times as fast as each kg of elephant.
The elephant has the highest rate per kg, because its greater surface area loses more heat.

questions.explanation: 720 ÷ 56 ≈ 13. The small mouse has a high SA:V, loses heat fast per kg, and so respires fast per kg.

questions.stem: An amoeba gets all its oxygen by diffusion across its cell-surface membrane. Why could a mouse not get enough oxygen by diffusion across its body surface alone?

options.text: A mouse has a smaller total surface area than an amoeba, so less oxygen can cross into its body.
A mouse has a much lower SA:V, and most of its cells lie too far from its surface for diffusion to supply them.
A mouse's cells are each much larger than an amoeba's cell, so every cell needs more oxygen than diffusion delivers.
Diffusion of oxygen can happen only in water, so a mouse on land cannot use it at any surface.
